sourceOfTruth: packages/vue-vscode live tree, joined to the VSC0 FeatureOwnershipMatrix and DesktopWebSharedBoundary and the BWH0 platform-host-services inventory; re-derived by tests/vscode-web/VSW0/vsw0.test.mjs
law: The web extension (vscode.dev / github.dev / browser-host mode) is one more consumer of the existing producers: every feature row below keeps its VSC0 owner and host-execution class, binds the DX0 receipt basis for browser-local execution, and reaches native capability only through the explicitly selected companion route. No row forks the desktop extension, gains a second semantic/type/project engine, or copies the whole extension to claim parity.

vocabulary.hostExecutionClass: DX0 host-execution-class.v1 enum (Portable | NativeOnly | ExternalOwner), reused verbatim
vocabulary.receiptBasis: DX0 product-receipt-basis.v1 fields (sourceRevisions, projectConfiguration, engineIdentity, hostIdentity, completenessState)

hostModes.definition: vscode.dev / github.dev with the extension's browser entry executing in the local web extension host (web workers). Semantic work rides the BWH wasm host through in-memory platform services.
VS Code desktop with the extension's main entry executing in the local Node extension host. This is the only shipped mode today.

Codespaces / SSH / WSL / tunnel remote workspace: the main entry executes in the remote Node extension host. A browser client viewing this workspace is a remote-native session, never browser-local parity.
hostModes.deliveryOwner: expansion.vscode-product (VSC train; the Node bundle runs unchanged remotely)

browserLocalReceipt.sourceRevisions: the virtual-workspace file revisions synchronized through the web VFS (VSW2); stale or wrong-handle results are rejected before display
browserLocalReceipt.projectConfiguration: the browser project profile: in-memory workspace identity, framework profile and configuration facts carried by the web host; no ambient filesystem reads exist in the browser closure
browserLocalReceipt.engineIdentity: the row's webEngine: the Verter compiler WASM build, the pinned browser TypeScript worker (ExternalOwner), or the explicitly selected companion engine with its exact version
browserLocalReceipt.hostIdentity: browser runtime plus WASM build selector (DX0 product-receipt-basis wasm-build-selector substrate); remote-native-only and companion-route rows override this field and may not claim it
browserLocalReceipt.completenessState: DX0 completenessStates; complete-empty is a successful empty answer; partial, pending, unsupported, ambiguous, failed, cancelled and stale are distinct and never published as complete

featureRows.note: declarative contributions ship unchanged from the web entry; the vue-postcss / vue-sugarss grammar gaps stay recorded exactly as VSC0 has them
presentation/pure tiers are already host-neutral (VSC0 boundary); the artifact stream comes from the wasm host's in-memory virtual workspace instead of the stdio LSP child
the webview panel and the sourcemap decode model are presentation/pure tiers; only the artifact producer is replaced by the wasm host
tree provider renders wasm-host analysis snapshots; the desktop provider tier's portable-path-only imports move to the browser entry at the VSW1 cutover, never a silent reclassification
demand-gated exactly as on desktop (verter.analysis.enabled, default off): closed/disabled views create no background semantic work in web mode either
the nine theme colors are static web-compatible contributions; binding facts come from the wasm host; the VSC4V retirement obligation is unchanged

featureRows.webEngine: pinned browser TypeScript worker (ExternalOwner) or the explicitly selected companion engine
featureRows.note: the desktop provider list does not silently apply in web mode: web offers only browser-admissible engines, and the selection is the execution-host selector owned by VSW4N

in-memory statistics over the wasm host; the persistence service is in-memory in the browser closure, so persistToFile / filePath settings surface the DX0 unsupported completeness state instead of being silently ignored
rides the wasm host's audit records; the presentation channel and pure transforms are already host-neutral

featureRows.hostIdentityOverride: authenticated local native companion (DX4/DX5 route) or the remote-native extension host; the browser closure has no process capability (BWH0 process service), so this row may not claim the browser-local receipt
featureRows.note: no child spawn exists in the web entry; the lm MCP definition is registered only when the companion or a remote-native host is actually serving, never as a dead definition
plugin injection follows the editor's engine wherever it runs; the carrier store the plugin reads is published through the web VFS (VSW2) instead of the stdio LSP store

featureRows.webEngine: Verter compiler WASM host (style structure requests)
featureRows.note: completion/hover/colors/highlights over wasm-host structure; preprocessor resolution is desktop-by-design (require.resolve) and surfaces unsupported in browser-local mode

featureRows.hostIdentityOverride: desktop or remote Node extension host (tsdk staging, relay staging and extension-hosted TypeScript service need fs/module provisioning); the browser-local engine binding is the pinned browser TypeScript worker (ExternalOwner) or the companion, selected by VSW4N
featureRows.note: the desktop provisioning tiers do not run in the web entry; no require() of project TypeScript exists in the browser closure
mirrors the VSC0 absent row: not shipped today, so a future snippet surface stays an explicit owner decision rather than an undocumented web gap

startupAdaptationInventory.nodeAssumption: activate() spawns the verter-lsp child through vscode-languageclient/node with stdio transport and binary discovery
startupAdaptationInventory.webRoute: the browser entry activates the same feature surface over the wasm host in a web worker (VSW1 worker transport); no child process exists

startupAdaptationInventory.nodeAssumption: typescriptServerPlugins runs inside the editor-owned engine; desktop stages tsdk and drives require()-based project TypeScript (engine tiers)
startupAdaptationInventory.webRoute: the plugin follows the editor's web TypeScript service; the pinned browser worker is the only embedded engine (ExternalOwner), VSW3

startupAdaptationInventory.nodeAssumption: verter-mcp is spawned as an attempt-owned child and registered through the lm provider API
startupAdaptationInventory.webRoute: no process capability: companion route only (VSW4N), or the remote-native host keeps owning the child

startupAdaptationInventory.nodeAssumption: tsdk staging, statistics persistence and claude-code detection read fs/os/process
startupAdaptationInventory.webRoute: in-memory platform services (BWH0 io/persistence); fs-bound settings surface unsupported in browser-local mode

startupAdaptationInventory.nodeAssumption: activationGate and startup ordering are pure decision logic shared by both entries
startupAdaptationInventory.webRoute: reused as-is from src/shared; the web entry is a sibling consumer, not a fork

rules: every VSC0 feature id has exactly one row here with a webDisposition from this vocabulary; a new desktop feature without a row is drift, not implicit coverage

a browser-local-route row must name its routeOwner in the VSW train and its webEngine; a remote-native-only or companion-route row must override hostIdentityOverride and may not claim the browserLocalReceipt hostIdentity
webDisposition changes are producer-owned ports with their own evidence, never relabels (VSC0 no-class-change-by-moving-code)
bwhServices cited by a row must exist in the BWH0 platform-host-services inventory

the web entry is placed at packages/vue-vscode/src/browser with host-neutral modules at packages/vue-vscode/src/shared and its suite at packages/vue-vscode/e2e/web (VSW1+ own those directories; VSW0 adds none of them)
acBasisDownstreamTestOwner: VSW1 owns the browser-entrypoint build admission and shared-code module-load runtime checks; VSW5 owns packaging, offline and browser-matrix qualification on real artifacts
acResourceRationale: VSW0 touches no hot paths and no UI: 0 production LOC across 0 files, so the WSP equal-work corpus and client-paint obligations do not apply here; real-client claims bind to VSW5
acExposureRegistration: DX1 owns the exposure-descriptor registration schema; no new operation is promoted by this contract node
